title: Testing the mettle of Mar Roxas
primary_topics: CJ enthusiastic endorsement of Mar Roxas appointment to the Department of Transportation and Communications as Patok! -- and why the DOTC is the most important government agency in the frontline of P-Noy war on poverty
The strategic importance of the DOTC: eight of 10 PPP projects plus the body politic arteries and nerve center
Three nettlesome infrastructure issues that will test Roxas mettle: NAIA 3/Piatco, North Luzon Railway, and LTO-Stradcom row
sub_topics: Pundits belittle DOTC as a ploy to checkmate Roxas; CJ says Patok! (perfect)
Roxas compared DOTC portfolio to body veins and arteries; CJ extends: not just arteries but nerve center directing the heart, muscles and limbs of the body politic

Personal friendship with P-Noy: forged in platinum; same mindset, same vision; Roxas set aside his own presidential ambitions and VP campaign to concentrate on P-Noy victory after Cory Aquino died; Roxas was constant companion and adviser during last 12 months as private citizen

DOTC handles eight of 10 PPP projects the government wants to bid out this year -- most important government agency in frontline of war on poverty; Roxas will be spark of economic recovery; President heads war on corruption, Roxas heads war on poverty (Very neat!)

First test: NAIA 3 -- festering 10 years; reached SC, Singapore ICC, Washington ICSID; RTC Pasay fixed just compensation for Piatco at $175M (vs Piatco demand of over $1B); Piatco will appeal; diplomatic problem (German government via Fraport); CJ suggests: consider abandoning terminal and constructing new one -- may be cheaper and faster and may convince Piatco to accept $175M since SC canceled its franchise in 2003

Second test: $1.8 billion, 80-km North Luzon Railway -- seven years in making, virtual standstill; DOTC wanted to renegotiate disadvantageous provisions with China National Machinery and Engineering Group; cannot just be rescinded because it involves the Chinese government (funding the project)
Third test: LTO row with Stradcom -- resulted in suspension of LTO chief Virginia Torres (allegedly P-Noy buddy); requires best political skills to mediate
Other issues: P11B roll-on roll-off seaports (France-funded), P7B radar control project (Japan-funded)
CJ conclusion: given Roxas demonstrated political, diplomatic and technocratic skills, he will come out the clean hero -- if he cannot solve these problems, wonder who can

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens with 'Patok!' (perfect) -- his verdict on Mar Roxas's appointment to the Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC), dismissing pundits who see it as a demotion. He extends Roxas's own metaphor of the DOTC as the body's 'veins and arteries': Roxas will steer not just the nation's arteries but 'the nerve center that directs the heart, muscles and limbs of the body politic.' Roxas's personal clout remains intact -- his friendship with P-Noy was 'forged in platinum'; Roxas set aside his own presidential ambitions and VP campaign after Cory Aquino's death to concentrate on P-Noy's victory. Strategically, the DOTC handles eight of 10 PPP projects -- making it the most important government agency in the frontline of the war on poverty: the President heads the war on corruption, Roxas heads the war on poverty ('Very neat!'). Three nettlesome tests: (1) NAIA 3 -- festering for 10 years across multiple forums (SC, Singapore ICC, Washington ICSID); RTC Pasay recently fixed just compensation for Piatco at $175M; CJ suggests considering abandoning the terminal and building new -- may be cheaper than years of litigation and may convince Piatco to accept the $175M since SC canceled its franchise in 2003; (2) the $1.8B North Luzon Railway (80km, 7 years in the making, virtual standstill) -- the diplomatic double lock (Chinese government funding) prevents simple rescission; and (3) the LTO-Stradcom row which resulted in the suspension of LTO chief Virginia Torres. CJ closes: given Roxas's demonstrated political, diplomatic, and technocratic skills, he will come out the clean hero -- 'If he cannot solve the problems, I wonder who can.'
